_readme: CORPUS SET NAME -> pokemontcg.io SET ID, for cards TCGdex has no scan for.
WHY THIS FILE IS CHECKED IN RATHER THAN FETCHED. api.pokemontcg.io answered
500 on two of three attempts while this was being built, and a sync that
depends on a flaky third party is a sync that silently drops images the next
time it hiccups. The set list moves a few times a year; this file is the
cheap, stable half. The per-card probe in sync-all-printings.mjs still runs
against the CDN, which is the reliable half.
EVERY ENTRY WAS PROVEN, NOT MATCHED BY NAME. A name match alone is a guess:
the name was used to propose the pairing, then up to four REAL card numbers
from that set were fetched from images.pokemontcg.io and the pairing was kept
only where one answered 200. 33 sets matched by name and 29 survived that.
THE FOUR THAT DID NOT, and they are not a bug to fix here: McDonald's
Collection 2014, 2015, 2017 and 2018 pair by name onto mcd14/mcd15/mcd17/
mcd18 and every card probe 404s, so that host does not actually carry them.
They stay imageless, which is the honest answer.
NUMBERS ARE NORMALISED, ONCE, AND IT MATTERS. The corpus writes Skyridge's
holos as H01 and this host serves them as H1, so a raw join lost all 32.
sync-all-printings.mjs tries the corpus number first and a de-padded form
second (H01 -> H1, 001 -> 1). 28 of the 29 sets need the raw form and only
Skyridge needs the other, which is why the fallback is tried second.
WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER. 1,929 English printings carry no TCGdex scan; these
29 sets are 784 of them. The largest hole left is Mega Rising at 331, which
is too new for this host, plus the promo sets and the trainer kits, whose
names do not correspond at all. Adding a set here means proving it the same
way: propose by name, then fetch real cards before believing it.
Generated and verified 1 September 2026.
